F01.evidence: This paper uses the steel surface defect detection public dataset NEU-DET [72], which includes a total of 1800 images of six types of defects, 300 images of each defect type, and the size of the image is 200 × 200 pixels.

F02.evidence: The number of training data sets is 1440, the number of verification data sets is 180, and the number of test data sets is 180.

F06.location: 4.1.2; validation set exists (180 images) but checkpoint selection criterion not stated

F07.evidence: For each category, all test images are sorted by confidence, and then each detection box is regarded as a positive example according to the confidence level from high to low

F09.location: 4.1; only raw dataset resolution 200x200 mentioned, network input size not reported

F10.evidence: For the simulations, the initial learning rate is set to 0.01, the Adam optimizer is used, the momentum is set to 0.937, the cosine function learning rate decay method is used, and the total epoch is 300 rounds.

F14.evidence: The experiments are conducted using the same equipment and training strategy to compare the performance of steel surface defect detection in terms of accuracy and lightweight on the NEU-DET dataset.

F15.location: 4.1.2, Table 5; no FPS or inference latency reported

main_result.evidence: Compared with the newly proposed YOLOv8 model, our model has a 4.69% accuracy improvement.
